artworks.title: Echo and Narcissus
artworks.description: Waterhouse pairs the fading nymph with the boy at the spring — Echo's last embrace refused, her body already dissolving into the repeating voice Ovid describes. Juno's punishment and Narcissus' scorn fixed her among the most famous unrequited loves of the Metamorphoses shelf.

artworks.title: Echo and Narcissus
artworks.description: Poussin's Louvre pastoral shows Narcissus already fading by the water while Echo collapses in grief and a putto mourns nearby — Ovid's double metamorphosis rendered as ordered landscape tragedy. The nymph who could only answer is left with nothing but sorrow beside the pool that destroyed her beloved. Oil on canvas, Musée du Louvre, Paris.

artworks.title: Echo Flying from Narcissus
artworks.description: The English Neoclassical painter Guy Head makes Echo the fleeing protagonist: she turns from the self-absorbed youth at the spring, her rejected love already driving her into the woods where only her voice will remain. Oil on canvas, Detroit Institute of Arts.

artworks.title: Narcissus and Echo
artworks.description: Turner's early mythological landscape dissolves Echo and Narcissus into luminous atmosphere — figures nearly lost in the golden haze of a classical Arcadia. The nymph's presence is felt as much as seen, a Romantic reading of Ovid in which voice and light outlast solid form. Oil on canvas, Tate, London.

artworks.title: The Nymph Echo
artworks.description: Le Moyne's marble isolates Echo alone — no Narcissus, no pool — a solitary nymph whose posture already hints at the wasting that will leave only her answering voice. Neoclassical sculpture as the myth reduced to a single figure. Musée du Louvre, Paris.

music.title: Écho et Narcisse
music.description: Gluck's Paris pastoral makes Echo the title nymph — cursed to answer, grieving the hunter at the pool, until Amour bends the myth toward a softer close.

popCulture.title: Echo
popCulture.description: English echo names the repeated sound after the nymph who could only answer — Ovid's curse turned into the ordinary word for a voice that comes back.

popCulture.title: Hades II
popCulture.creator: Supergiant Games
popCulture.description: Supergiant's sequel brings Echo into Melinoë's underworld war — the answering nymph as a living remnant of Narcissus' story.
